subject: paediatrics
title: Trisomy 18, Trisomy 13 and Sex Chromosome Aneuploidies

steps.tx: Severe autosomal aneuploidies beyond trisomy 21 present with profound multisystem malformations and early lethality. The second most prevalent autosomal trisomy in liveborn neonates is **Edwards syndrome trisomy 18**, occurring in roughly one in six thousand births with a marked three-to-one female predominance. Complete maternal meiotic nondisjunction accounts for over ninety percent of cases, producing severe intrauterine growth restriction and early neonatal mortality.
steps.say: Edwards syndrome, or trisomy eighteen, is the second most common autosomal trisomy. It features severe growth restriction, multiple congenital anomalies, and early mortality within the first year.

rows: Median survival under 14 days; >90% die by 1 year
Median survival 3 to 10 days; >90% die by 1 year

steps.tx: Neonatal physical examination reveals pathognomonic craniofacial and extremity abnormalities. Classic stigmata of trisomy 18 include a prominent occiput, microcephaly, micrognathia, low-set malformed ears, a short sternum, and characteristic **clenched hands with overlapping fingers** where the index finger overlaps the third and the fifth finger overlaps the fourth. The feet exhibit rocker-bottom contours with prominent calcanei and hypoplastic nails.
steps.say: Trisomy eighteen presents with a prominent occiput, small jaw, and clenched hands where index and fifth fingers overlap middle digits, alongside rocker-bottom feet.

right.title: Trisomy 18 Extremity Signs
points: Clenched fists with overlapping index over 3rd

steps.tx: Defective midline development of the forebrain and face characterises the third major autosomal trisomy. Arising from triplication of chromosome 13, **Patau syndrome trisomy 13** reflects a failure of prechordal mesoderm development resulting in holoprosencephaly. Neonates present with severe microcephaly, microphthalmia or anophthalmia, cleft lip and palate, postaxial hexadactyly, and scalp cutis aplasia displaying punched-out skin defects in the parieto-occipital scalp.
steps.say: Patau syndrome, or trisomy thirteen, causes midline brain defects, microphthalmia, cleft lip and palate, postaxial polydactyly, and scalp cutis aplasia, with mortality exceeding ninety percent.

steps.tx: Sex chromosome aneuploidy in phenotypic females provokes short stature and gonadal failure. The condition **Turner syndrome 45X** results from complete or partial loss of the second sex chromosome, with paternal sex chromosome loss accounting for eighty percent of cases. Because both X chromosomes are required for oocyte maintenance, premature follicular atresia produces fibrous streak ovaries, manifesting as primary amenorrhoea and lack of secondary sexual characteristics.
steps.say: Turner syndrome features a 45,X karyotype from missing paternal sex chromosomes. Ovarian follicular atresia produces streak gonads, causing primary amenorrhoea and pubertal failure.

vis.caption: Phenotypic features of Turner syndrome showing webbed neck, streak ovaries, and short stature. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Haploinsufficiency of pseudoautosomal genes impairs linear skeletal growth. The universal feature of Turner syndrome is **short stature SHOX deficiency**, caused by loss of one copy of the Short Stature Homeobox gene on the X chromosome pseudoautosomal region. Other somatic stigmata include a webbed neck (pterygium colli) arising from nuchal cystic hygroma, low posterior hairline, shield chest with wide-spaced nipples, cubitus valgus, and neonatal lymphedema.
steps.say: Short stature in Turner syndrome results from SHOX gene loss. Physical stigmata include webbed neck, low hairline, broad shield chest, cubitus valgus, and pedal lymphedema at birth.

left.title: Cardiovascular Lesions in Turner
points: Coarctation of the aorta (10% of patients)
Dilatation and dissection of thoracic aorta

steps.tx: Structured endocrine therapies optimize final adult height and secondary sexual maturation. Management of Turner syndrome requires early subcutaneous **recombinant growth hormone** therapy initiated around four to six years of age to counteract SHOX-mediated growth failure and optimize final adult height. Low-dose oral estradiol therapy is introduced around twelve years of age to induce breast budding, followed by cycling with progesterone to establish withdrawal bleeding.
steps.say: Treat Turner syndrome with recombinant growth hormone from four years to improve adult height. Introduce low-dose estrogen at twelve years followed by progesterone to induce puberty.

steps.tx: The most prevalent sex chromosome aneuploidy in phenotypic males produces hypogonadism and tall stature. Affecting one in six hundred males, **Klinefelter syndrome 47XXY** results from nondisjunction of sex chromosomes during parental gametogenesis. Affected boys present after puberty with tall eunuchoid proportions, long extremities, sparse body hair, bilateral gynecomastia, and pathognomonic small, firm hyalinized testes with a volume under four millilitres.
steps.say: Klinefelter syndrome features a 47,XXY karyotype. Post-pubertal boys present with tall stature, long limbs, bilateral gynecomastia, and small firm testes with azoospermia.

left.title: Hormonal Profile in Klinefelter
points: Elevated serum FSH (loss of Sertoli inhibin)

right.title: Long-Term Health Risks
points: 20-fold increased risk of male breast cancer

steps.tx: Cytogenetic confirmation establishes definitive diagnosis across all numerical and structural chromosomal syndromes. Performing a standard **diagnostic G-banded karyotype** from peripheral blood lymphocytes visualizes metaphase chromosomes, confirming trisomies 18 and 13 as well as 45,X and 47,XXY. Karyotyping differentiates free non-disjunction trisomies from translocations, which is essential for accurate genetic counselling and recurrence risk estimation for families.
steps.say: G-banded karyotyping provides definitive genetic confirmation of trisomy eighteen, thirteen, Turner, and Klinefelter syndromes, allowing precise family genetic counselling and recurrence planning.

rows: Low recurrence risk in subsequent pregnancies
